questions.question: What does an individual model consist of?

result.answer:
The overall model consists of individual Bayesian models for each language, plus crosslingual latent variables to incorporate soft role agreement between aligned constituents. [1]
In this model, the latent variables are part of the model itself rather than an external penalty, enabling standard Bayesian learning methods such as sampling. [2]
By contrast, a related prior model (Titov and Khapra's cross-lingual SRL work) has separate monolingual models for each language and an extra penalty term. [3]
